requested.title: Live-reload WebSocket upgrade accepts any Origin (dev server reachable from any website)
Island props resolved by tree order across independent renders — a page island can hydrate with a server island's props
Island props taken from any DOM element matching a predictable global id
Island fetch follows redirects and the response body is written to innerHTML unverified
Unvalidated attribute resolved into a dynamic import() sink, anchored on the clobberable document.baseURI
A CSS URL is marked loaded before the stylesheet loads, so one transient failure permanently unstyles every other island sharing it
pinGlobal state keys are DOM-clobberable, letting injected markup disable island hydration and amplify island-endpoint requests

parsedVerdicts.reasoning: Verified end-to-end. `liveReloadHandler` (dev/devWatcher.ts:152-172) builds a URL, reads the attacker-chosen `entry` query param, and calls `srv.upgrade(req, …)` with no inspection of the `Origin` header. The route is injected straight into Bun's `routes` map (devWatcher.ts:635, 738, 821), so it never reaches `buildRequestContext` — and even if it did, `KIND_POLICY.ws` has `csrf: false`, and `csrfCheck` only gates unsafe methods, so a GET handshake would pass regardless. It also bypasses user `handle` middleware, which is only invoked at Mochi.ts:991 (page), 1240 (api) and 1922 (fallback `fetch`), and bypasses the protection gate and rate limiter. On open (Mochi.ts:1955-1964) the server immediately sends `liveReloadGreeting(client.data.__mochiEntry)`, and liveReloadGeneration.ts:31 computes `unscopedReloads + (scopedReloads.get(entry) ?? 0)` — a genuine per-absolute-path oracle driven entirely by attacker input — while `onDevEmailRecorded` (Mochi.ts:1979-1987) fans `email:new:<id>` to every socket in the unbounded `liveReloadClients` Set. So a hostile page a developer visits can complete the handshake and read save-activity timing, dev-outbox ids and the boot id. Impact is correctly bounded by the finding: `startDevWatcher` only runs when `development` is true (Mochi.ts:2151), the `message` handler answers only `ping`→`pong` so the socket is read-only, no source or file contents are exposed, and the email viewer bodies stay unreadable cross-origin — I confirmed there is not a single `Access-Control-Allow-*` header anywhere in packages/mochi/src. The deployed dev-mode image sets `MOCHI_LIVE_RELOAD=false` (Dockerfile:61), which drops the `wsHandlersMap` entry so an upgraded socket receives nothing. MEDIUM is a fair rating for a dev-host CSWSH/info-leak, and the suggested fix (compare `Origin` against `resolveExpectedOrigin`) is already available in runtime/proxy.ts.

Every link in the chain checks out. Ids are allocated per render with no namespacing: `emitIslandProps` returns `mochi-props-${ctx.islandProps.size}` (islands/islandPropsRegistry.ts:47), `renderComponent` clears `ctx.islandProps` per render (ComponentRegistry.ts:1704), and the island endpoint runs through `buildRequestContext`, which creates a fresh `islandProps: new Map()` per request (runtime/requestSetup.ts:146) — so an island fragment restarts at `mochi-props-0`. The endpoint calls the same `registry.renderComponent` (Mochi.ts:1620), whose HTMLRewriter pass calls `injectIslandPropsBlock` (ComponentRegistry.ts:1775), and nothing in the endpoint tail (Mochi.ts:1654-1694) strips those blocks; I confirmed `idPrefix` only reaches Svelte's `render()` and never touches props ids. The preprocessor emits `props-ref` for every `mochi:hydrate`/`mochi:hydrate:visible`/`mochi:clientOnly:visible` site with non-empty props (svelteAstPreprocess.ts:240, 382), including nested ones inside a server island, so collisions are guaranteed whenever both renders emit at least one payload. The lookup defect is exactly as described: `scope?.querySelector(...) ?? document.getElementById(ref)` falls through on a *miss* as well as on a null scope, and for a page island (`closest()` null) the only lookup is the document-wide, tree-order one. The commit that introduced this file (ea1c97bd, #340) fixed only the nested→page direction and its test file covers only page-block-first ordering, so the reverse order is untested and unguarded. The in-repo shape is already present: `DemoPage.svelte` renders `<ReadmeCopy mochi:hydrate …>` above the demo children and `<CodeViewer {sources} mochi:hydrate />` below them, while `nested-islands/DeferWithHydrators.svelte` nests three props-carrying `mochi:hydrate` Counters inside a `mochi:defer` island — so CodeViewer's `props-ref` collides with a Counter's block that is earlier in tree order once the fragment lands. Eager islands usually win the race (the bootstrap is a deferred module at Mochi.ts:367 while the inline ServerIsland classic script at 368 starts fetching during parse), but a below-the-fold `mochi:hydrate:visible` island resolves props only in the IntersectionObserver callback (HydratableIsland.ts:43 → 75-78), which is deterministically after the fetch. Outcome is a devalue throw (HydratableIsland.ts:123) leaving a production-hidden `mochi-island-failure` stub appended, or silent hydration with another component's props. HIGH_BUG is appropriate.

The code claim is accurate and I confirmed it: `resolveIslandProps` takes `block?.textContent` from whatever node answers `document.getElementById('mochi-props-N')` (or `scope.querySelector('#…')`), with no check that the node is the framework's own `<script type="application/json">`, no `data-` marker and no binding between island and payload, and the ids are fully predictable because `emitIslandProps` numbers them from the per-request map size. Window/document id lookup is tree-order, so an injected element with that id placed above the real block does supply the props, and `devalueParse` on non-devalue text throws into `_doHydrate`'s catch (a hidden failure stub, i.e. a per-island DoS) while a crafted devalue payload yields full props control. What I cannot confirm is reachability. There is no path in this repository where a request-controlled value becomes an element `id`: the only `id={…}` interpolations are `EmailViewer/EmailList.svelte:16` (framework-generated outbox ids, dev-only) and a demo's Pokémon id; the only user-content HTML sink is the HN demo, and `packages/demos/src/hn/hn-sanitize.ts` is a strict allowlist (p/a/i/b/code/pre) that deletes every attribute except a URL-parsed `href`, so no `id` survives; and `rehype-slug` is applied only to repo-authored docs/mdsvex markdown, not to user submissions. So exploitability rests entirely on a downstream consumer rendering user HTML through a sanitizer that preserves `id` (DOMPurify's default does) with an island above which that content sits, and ideally a prop that reaches `{@html}` — plausible, but unverifiable from this repo. I deliberately did not mark this a duplicate of F2 even though it is the same line: the two defects are independent, since namespacing the server-island ids would not add node verification, and requiring `HTMLScriptElement && type === 'application/json'` would not help F2 (the colliding server-island block passes that test). Treat it as worthwhile hardening (attribute-based selector the framework owns) rather than a confirmed vulnerability; I left the severity as reported rather than confirm it.

The mechanical observations are right — `_fetchContent` fetches with default options (`redirect: 'follow'`, ServerIsland.ts:161), ignores `response.redirected`/`response.url`/`Content-Type`, assigns the body to `this.innerHTML` (187), and then `import()`s the specifier named by the first element's bootstrap marker (193-196) — but I could not find any way for that request to be answered off-origin, and the finding concedes this. The URL is built from `data-asset-prefix`, which the preprocessor emits as the `__MOCHI_ASSET_PREFIX__` placeholder (svelteAstPreprocess.ts:300, 318) resolved from `registry.assetPrefix`, i.e. `normalizeAssetPrefix()` output: a rooted path with no scheme, whitespace or `..` segments (utils/index.ts:145-168) and never request-derived. On the server side the island route sits directly in `bunRoutes` (Mochi.ts:1559), so it never runs user `handle` middleware (applied only at Mochi.ts:991/1240/1922); `KIND_POLICY.island` sets `trailingSlash: false` and `csrf: false` (runtime/requestSetup.ts:67), so no normalization redirect is possible; the protection gate's non-page branch returns a plain 403 body (protection/gate.ts:135), and 4xx sets `abort: true` so the retry budget is not even spent. The only off-origin route I found is a developer writing `assetPrefix: '//evil.example'`, which slips through `normalizeAssetPrefix` as a protocol-relative path — a self-inflicted misconfiguration, not attacker input. That leaves this as defense-in-depth against a hypothetical edge/CDN open redirect in front of `/_mochi/island/*`, where the attacker would already control the origin's routing. The hardening (`redirect: 'error'`, assert `new URL(response.url).origin === location.origin`, check `Content-Type`) is cheap and I'd support it, but there is no exploitable condition in this codebase today.

The description of the sink is accurate: `resolveComponentUrl` does `new URL(componentUrl, baseURI).href` with no scheme/origin constraint (resolveComponentUrl.ts:6), its only caller feeds it to `await import(...)` (HydratableIsland.ts:109) with `componentUrl = this.getAttribute('component-url')` and `document.baseURI`, absolute-URL passthrough is pinned by resolveComponentUrl.test.ts:25-27 to support a CDN `assetPrefix`, and baseURI anchoring was a deliberate 0.10.0 change (commit 77b76bc8, docs/183-production-builds.md). But both exploitation paths require a pre-existing HTML-injection primitive in which *unknown custom elements with arbitrary attributes* (or a `<base>` tag) survive sanitization — a far narrower precondition than F3's `id`-only requirement. Every allowlist sanitizer rejects both: DOMPurify's default ALLOWED_TAGS contains neither custom elements nor `base`, `sanitize-html` is likewise an allowlist, and the only sanitizer in this repo (`packages/demos/src/hn/hn-sanitize.ts`) deletes any tag outside p/a/i/b/code/pre and every attribute but `href`. In the remaining case — an app with no sanitizer at all — the attacker already has direct script execution, and Mochi cannot contain it: docs/72-hydratable.md:64 documents that `'unsafe-inline'` is required because there is no CSP nonce wiring, and `unsafe-inline` permits injected inline scripts and event handlers. `component-url` itself is never request-derived; it is emitted from the `__MOCHI_COMPONENT_URL__<key>__` placeholder resolved against `componentEntryUrls` (ComponentRegistry.ts:1721). So the gadget adds nothing an injector does not already have under any sanitizer configuration I can reasonably posit, which is why I rate it not exploitable. The proposed allowlist check (origin + `assetPrefix + '/client/'`) is still sensible hardening and would need to keep the documented CDN-prefix case working.

Confirmed by reading the whole path. The tracker's contract is 'in the pool means loaded' (sharedCssTracker.ts:9-15), but HydratableIsland.ts:94-104 calls `markLoadedCss(cssUrl)` *before* awaiting the `<link>`, and the `onerror` branch rejects (101) without removing the URL from the pool or the element from `document.head`. The rejection propagates out of `_doHydrateInner`, is caught by `_doHydrate` (58-65), and because `_hydrated = true` was set at line 54 before the attempt, `connectedCallback`'s guard at 35 means that island is never retried — permanently non-interactive, with the appended `mochi-island-failure` stub `display:none` in production (islandFailureStub.ts:5). Meanwhile sibling islands see `isLoadedCss(cssUrl) === true`, skip the load entirely, and hydrate fully interactive but unstyled. The shared-URL precondition is real: `css-url` is `__MOCHI_CSS_URL__<islandKey>__` (svelteAstPreprocess.ts:251, 386) resolved from `cssFileUrls.get(h.resolvedPath)` (ComponentRegistry.ts:1723-1730), so every instance of the same `mochi:hydrate:visible`/`mochi:clientOnly:visible` component on a page carries an identical URL. ServerIsland.ts:174-181 re-implements the same optimistic mark against the same global pool with no `onerror` at all, so a server island whose CSS 404s poisons the pool for later hydratable islands too. The secondary FOUC effect is also real, since a flag rather than a promise means a concurrent island skips the await while the stylesheet is still in flight. I'm adjusting severity from BUG to BUG unchanged in substance — this is a correctness/robustness defect with no security impact, triggered by a transient CSS failure rather than by an attacker; the memoized-promise fix in the recommendation is the right shape.

The clobbering mechanism is confirmed and deterministic. `pinGlobal` does `slot[key] ??= factory()` with `slot = globalThis` and no type check (utils/globalState.ts:5-9); in a browser realm the Window named-properties object exposes every element with a non-empty `id` as a window property, so if `

` exists the read returns an Element, `??=` skips the assignment, and `pool` is an HTMLElement. Ordering works out: the shell puts all scripts after `{{mochi.body}}` (templates/default-shell.html), the island bundle is a deferred `type="module"` script (Mochi.ts:367) and even the inline classic ServerIsland script (368) runs after the body is parsed, so the clobbered property already exists. The downstream effects are as described: `isLoadedCss` throws a TypeError inside `_doHydrateInner`, caught at HydratableIsland.ts:58 so every `css-url`-bearing island renders the failure stub; ServerIsland.ts:9 duplicates the same global access inline and its `_css.has(cssUrl)` sits *after* the fetch inside the try block, so each of the 10 attempts (`maxRetries` 9 → `attempt <= 10`, ~27s of backoff — the finding's '11 times over ~30s' is marginally overstated) performs a real island-endpoint request before throwing. `__mochi_visibility_pool__` (sharedVisibilityObserver.ts:19, called uncaught from `connectedCallback`) and the two `deferInvalidation.ts` pins (13, 38) share the root cause. What I cannot establish is reachability: the precondition is identical to F3's — attacker-influenced `id` in rendered HTML — and no such path exists in this repo (the HN sanitizer strips all attributes; `rehype-slug` runs only on repo-authored markdown; no request data reaches an `id`). Impact is availability/request-amplification against the victim's own page, and in the DOMPurify-default scenario that makes it reachable, an `` loop would already give an injector comparable amplification. Genuine, cheap hardening (symbol key or an `instanceof Set` check), but not a confirmed vulnerability; severity left as reported rather than endorsed.
